chunks: Al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad al-Ashʿarī, from Muʿallā ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī al-Washshāʾ, from Ḥammād ibn ʿUthmān, from ʿAbd al-Aʿlā ibn Aʿyan, who said:
I heard Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام saying: “With me are the weapons of Rasūl Allāh صلى الله عليه وآله, concerning which I am not disputed.”
Then he عليه السلام said: “Surely the weapon is protected from him; if it were placed with the worst of Allah’s creation, he would become the best of them.”

Then he عليه السلام said: “Surely this affair comes to the one for whom the jaw is turned; then when there is Allah’s will concerning him in it, he emerges, and the people say: ‘What is this that has happened?’ And Allah places for him a hand upon the heads of his subjects.”

key_terms.السِّلَاحَ: the weapon, mentioned as something specially protected and significant
key_terms.الْمَشِيئَةُ: the divine will or decree by which the matter comes to realization
key_terms.خَرَجَ: he emerges or rises forth when Allah’s will is realized
key_terms.رَسُولِ اللَّهِ: the Messenger of Allah, Muḥammad صلى الله عليه وآله
key_terms.رَعِيَّتِهِ: his subjects or flock, meaning the people under his authority
key_terms.سِلَاحُ: the weaponry of Rasūl Allāh صلى الله عليه وآله, serving here as a sign of divinely designated authority
key_terms.هَذَا الْأَمْرَ: this affair, referring in context to the divinely designated authority

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith describe the signs of the Imam’s authority and Allah’s support for his leadership?
ai.summary: This hadith states that the weapons of Rasūl Allāh صلى الله عليه وآله are among the signs held by the Imam and are not open to dispute. It also indicates that the affair of authority belongs to the one chosen by Allah, whose emergence may surprise people, and whose rule is aided by divine support over his community.

en.hubeali: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad Al Ashary, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Al Washa, from Hammad Bin Usman, from Abdul A’ala Bin Ayn who said,
‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘With me<sup>asws</sup> are the weapons of Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>, there is no dispute with regards to it’.
Then he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The weapons are defended from. If these were placed with the most evil creature of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, he would be the best of them’.

Then he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘This matter (Divine Authority) comes to be to the one for whom the jaws would drop, so when it would be the Desire from Allah<sup>azwj</sup> with regards to it, so the people would be saying, ‘What is this which has happened?’ And Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Place for him<sup>asws</sup>, and Hand upon the heads of his<sup>asws</sup> citizens’.
en.sarwar: 2. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Asha‘ari has narrated from Mu‘alla ibn Muhammad from al-Hassan ibn Ali al-Washsha’ from Hammad ibn ‘Uthman from ‘Abdallah ‘Ala’ ibn A‘yan who has said that he heard abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) say the following.
“With me is the arms of the Messenger of Allah. It is not disputable.”
The Imam (a.s.) then said, “The Arms are well defended. If they would be place with the worst creature of Allah he will be very good among them.”

The Imam (a.s.) then said, “This matter (leadership with Divine authority) will proceed to the one who will enjoy total obedience. When Allah’s will grant permission he will appear in public and people will say, “What is this happening?” Allah will make his hand to protect his followers and subjects.”
